original_question: Investigate whether the dense-orbit and invariant-measure phenomena discussed above persist for biholomorphisms of Cn and for volume-preserving or symplectic automorphisms of Cn.
target_in_paper: Section 9, Problem 9.4: "Explore the above properties for the following classes of maps in C^n: biholomorphisms of C^n and volume preserving (resp. symplectic) automorphisms of C^n (resp. C^n with even n)."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly points to the dynamics-on-map-spaces part of the paper, correctly isolates the two phenomena being referenced from the preceding discussion in Section 9 (dense orbits and invariant measures), and correctly names the map classes singled out in Problem 9.4: biholomorphisms of C^n, volume-preserving automorphisms of C^n, and symplectic automorphisms in the even-dimensional case.
missing_details: The exact target is Problem 9.4 in Section 9, not a broader foliation problem elsewhere in the paper.

The phrase "discussed above" should be unpacked: in the immediately preceding Section 9 context, the two properties are (i) existence of a dense orbit and (ii) extension of B. Weiss's construction of invariant probability measures.
The ambient spaces in Section 9 are endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets (the compact-open topology), and that setup should be carried into a stand-alone formulation.
The problem concerns spaces of holomorphic automorphisms of C^n, not arbitrary holomorphic self-maps or maps between unrelated manifolds.
The symplectic case is only meaningful in even complex dimension; the paper explicitly restricts it to the even-dimensional case.

To make the question self-contained, one should say what "volume-preserving" and "symplectic" mean: preservation of the standard holomorphic volume form on C^n and of a fixed standard holomorphic symplectic form on C^{2m}.

Problem 9.4 is intentionally terse and refers back to earlier Section 9 context; a faithful rewrite should not impose a different action or broaden the question beyond asking for analogues of those two Section 9 phenomena for these three automorphism classes.
refined_question: Equip the spaces Aut(C^n), Aut_vol(C^n) = {F in Aut(C^n) : F^*(dz_1∧...∧dz_n) = dz_1∧...∧dz_n}, and, when n = 2m, Aut_sp(C^{2m}) = {F in Aut(C^{2m}) : F^*omega = omega for a fixed standard holomorphic symplectic form omega}, with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. In the sense of Section 9—namely, as analogues of the dense-orbit question and the Weiss-type invariant-probability-measure question previously posed for spaces of holomorphic maps—do these automorphism spaces exhibit the same two phenomena: existence of a dense orbit and existence of invariant probability measures of Weiss type?
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at Section 9, Problem 9.4, because it reproduces the same three classes of maps and the same two phenomena referred to by the paper's phrase "the above properties." Those properties are identified just above Problem 9.4: the introductory Section 9 discussion recalls Birkhoff's dense-orbit phenomenon and Weiss's invariant probability measures, and Problem 9.3 reformulates them as the dense-orbit question and the extension of Weiss's construction. Problem 9.4 itself is deliberately brief, so the only paper-faithful sharpening is to make that Section 9 context explicit, retain the compact-open topology used there, and add the paper's even-dimensional restriction in the symplectic case, without introducing broader variants or a new dynamical setup not specified in the paper.
